articles.title: Habeeb Ogunneye signs for Arsenal
articles.excerpt: The talented young full-back joins with senior experience
articles.content:
We're pleased to announce the signing of talented young full-back Habeeb Ogunneye.

Habeeb joins us with experience from Manchester United and Newport County, as well as England's under-17s side. 

"It feels great to be here, it's such a big club," Habeeb said after putting pen to paper on his Arsenal contract. 

Born in Hackney, our new defender was drawn to a return to north London. "I've got family who live in Hackney, so it's literally a full-circle moment. It's fantastic [to have my family here]," he added.

It wasn't just his own family connections that made Arsenal the destination of choice for Habeeb. 

The young full-back has been impressed by the number of academy players who have progressed to our first team, especially after seeing them involved in our Premier League title triumph last season. 

"When I heard [Arsenal] were interested in me, I said to my agents it's a no-brainer. Seeing all the young players that are coming through as well, so I just wanted to come straight away. 

"I just wanted to be part of that group, and win games together. It's good playing with good players, good defenders; it's only going to better you."

In addition to his academy experience at Manchester United, Habeeb has senior experience, having spent the first half of last season on loan at Newport County. The full-back scored for The Exiles and ultimately helped them fight off relegation. 

"It was great, my first season in men's football, [learning about] the physicality, the recovery side, it was a great experience. 

"I remember when I scored, it was like a moment of madness. I didn't really know what to do. The stadium erupted; that's the first time it's properly happened for me, being in a big stadium where the three points mean something."

With plenty of experience already in his career, Habeeb hopes to get off to a good start at Arsenal and take his game to the next level. 

"[Now] I want to get better every day and we'll see what happens from there." 

Everyone at Arsenal is delighted to welcome Habeeb to the club and looks forward to seeing him in action.

articles.title: The jury's options in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial
articles.excerpt: Jurors have five options before them as they decide the fate of the former nurse charged with killing her three children.
articles.content:
• Published
    31 August 2026, 12:17 BST

Lindsay Clancy's murder trial has gripped the American public for the last five weeks.

The 36-year-old former nurse killed her three small children in the basement of their family home in Massachusetts.

Charged with three counts of first-degree murder, she does not dispute killing her two sons and daughter in 2023.

But her lawyer argues she was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time, and therefore could not distinguish right from wrong.

The prosecution, on the other hand, argues Clancy made a calculated, intentional decision to kill them and knew right from wrong in that moment.

On Monday morning, a jury of nine women and three men will continue to deliberate, with several options before them:

  • not guilty

  • not guilty by reason of insanity

  • first-degree murder

  • second-degree murder

  • manslaughter

not guilty

not guilty by reason of insanity

first-degree murder

second-degree murder

manslaughter

Not guilty / not guilty by reason of insanity

This hinges on the postpartum psychosis defence - her legal team argued that Clancy hallucinated a voice after giving birth to her youngest child that told her to kill the children.

Expert witnesses told the court how severe this illness can be, and family members testified about Clancy's state of mind.

Under Massachusetts law, there is no burden on Clancy to prove her mental illness and that she lacked criminal responsibility.

Rather, it is on the prosecution to prove beyond reasonable doubt that she was criminally responsible when she killed her children, criminal defence lawyer Elyse Hershon told the BBC.

They can do this by either proving beyond reasonable doubt that she didn't suffer from a mental illness at the time or that, while she had a mental illness, she still controlled her actions and knew they were wrong.

A not guilty verdict would mean Clancy went free but that is considered highly unlikely. Much more likely is a not guilty by reason of insanity, which would result in Clancy being detained at a hospital.

"The case really comes down to where she is going to serve the rest of her life; the defence thinks it should be a psychiatric facility, the prosecution thinks it should be in a state prison," Hershon said.

Watch: What is postpartum psychosis and why is it central in the Lindsay Clancy trial?

First-degree murder

This is the most serious potential outcome for Clancy - being found guilty of first-degree murder, which is the intentional and premeditated killing of another person.

In the state of Massachusetts, this conviction carries a mandatory sentence of life in prison without the possibility of parole.

As Heather Cucolo, a New York Law School professor and expert in mental health law, put it to the BBC, Clancy would effectively need to be seen as "a monster in the jury's eyes" if they pick this outcome.

Jurors would have to find there was extreme atrocity or cruelty or premeditation or both to convict Clancy of this, and it would mean the prosecution had proven there were no mitigating factors.

In this case, mental disease or defect - as the law describes it - could be a mitigating factor.

Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague said during closing arguments there was no dispute Clancy was suffering from mental illness but it was not so severe that she didn't know right from wrong.

Expert witnesses for the prosecution cast doubt on whether Clancy actually heard the voice that she said ordered her to kill her children.

Second-degree murder

This is a catch-all for any murder that is not first-degree, under Massachusetts law.

It applies to unlawful killings committed with malice or extreme recklessness, but without prior planning.

"For this verdict, the jurors may not be convinced that the actions leading up to the murder rose to the level of pre-planned [or] premeditated but that instead, Clancy consciously saw an opportunity to commit the killings at the specified time," Cucolo said.

In the case of second-degree murder, Clancy would also face a life sentence - but with the possibility of parole.

Manslaughter

The jury received yet another option when the judge allowed them to find Clancy guilty of manslaughter - previously a point of contention between the defence and the prosecution.

Manslaughter, which is defined as causing death by an unintentional, mistaken or neglectful act, carries a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison per count.

Intent is an important distinction between a verdict like manslaughter and the two murder verdicts, experts said.

"This option allows the jury to accept that the murders were not planned or calculated but that instead Clancy made a split-second decision to act," Cucolo said.

The prosecution is not obligated to demonstrate that she intended to cause the children's deaths for there to be a manslaughter conviction, she added.

articles.title: Sunderland reopen talks with Tottenham for Danso
articles.excerpt: Sunderland reopen talks with Tottenham for Danso
articles.content:
• Published
    30 August 2026

Sunderland have reopened talks with Tottenham over a permanent move for defender Kevin Danso.

BBC Sport revealed on Friday night that Sunderland had a loan offer rejected by Spurs for the Austria international.

But the Black Cats have returned to the table and opened discussions over a permanent offer for Danso.

Personal terms are not said to be an issue for Danso if the clubs agree a fee.

Club-to-club talks are progressing but as of yet there is no agreement.

Tottenham are likely to require a replacement before sanctioning an exit for Danso, with manager Roberto De Zerbi wanting that player to have Premier League experience.

Danso was signed on loan from Lens in January 2025 and the deal was made permanent later that year with Spurs paying the French club £20.9m.

Sunderland are also interested in signing Lyon winger Malick Fofana after previously making an offer for Marseille's Igor Paixao.

Fofana, 21, is open to a move to the Stadium of Light after being linked with a switch to Roma earlier this summer.

However, the Belgian is just one of a number of options being considered by Sunderland. Paixao has been the subject of a formal bid, while the Black Cats have also been linked with Manchester City winger Jack Grealish.

Grealish is understood to be prioritising a move to Everton, despite attracting interest from his boyhood club Aston Villa.

Sunderland are also keen on signing a centre-back before Tuesday's transfer deadline.

articles.title: Wrexham rip up player's contract after playing just six games for club
articles.excerpt: Conor Coady is reportedly set to leave Wrexham and become a free agent before the transfer window closes.
articles.content:
• Martha Riley
  • Published: 15:11, 31 Aug 2026
  • Updated: 15:11, 31 Aug 2026

Conor Coady has become a free agent following his departure from Wrexham, the club have confirmed.

The ex-England international joined the Welsh outfit from Leicester last summer in a £2million deal, penning a two-year contract.

But Coady has struggled for game time since then, making just six appearances in all competitions for the club.

He spent the second half of the season on loan at Charlton and featured 12 times as the Addicks secured Championship safety.

The centre-back later then to Wrexham for the new season, but was

Coady hasn't been included in the matchday squad for all four of the Hollywood-owned outfit's games so far this term.

And his time in north Wales has now come to a premature end, with the club announcing the news on social media.

End of the road

In a post on X, Wrexham wrote: "We can confirm that Conor Coady has left the Club following the mutual termination of his contract.

"We wish Conor all the best for the future."

No further details were given on where the former Wolves captain could go next, although Welsh rivals Swansea have previously been credited with an interest.

An early departure from the Racecourse Ground is a far from ideal scenario for Coady, who admitted earlier this summer he hadn't given up hope of a revival at Wrexham.

Having joined the Red Dragons ahead of their return to the Championship following a third consecutive promotion, he moved to Phil Parkinson's side with the Premier League in his sights.

Speaking in May, Coady said: "When I went there last summer, it was something I really wanted to be a part of and sometimes I think people look at footballers and think something's happened.

"Nothing's ever personal in football. Sometimes a manager just doesn't take to you and I think that was what it was.

"[But] I've got a really good relationship with Phil Parkinson - nothing's ever happened between us.

"I had a great relationship when I was there and they were brilliant with me in January when it came to maybe wanting to leave if there was an opportunity.

"Wrexham is a brilliant, brilliant club so I can't sit here now and rule anything out because I don't know what's going to happen."

Conor Coady's career

With Coady now a free agent, there will no doubt be plenty of clubs keen to take on a player with his wealth of experience.

The 33-year-old has made 198 Premier League appearances and captained Wolves in the top flight.

He skippered the West Midlands side to promotion from the Championship in 2018 and held onto the armband.

Coady also has almost 200 Championship appearances to his name, having joined Huddersfield on a permanent deal in 2014 after starting his senior career at Liverpool.

He then made the switch to Wolves, where he went on to play over 300 games for the club across an eight-year spell, earning 10 senior England caps during this time too.

His time at the club came to an end in 2023, as he fell out of favour and secured a loan switch to Everton.

Coady then left permanently a year later to join Leicester, where he helped the Foxes win the Championship title.

But following their immediate relegation from the Premier League in 2025 he made the move to Wrexham.

articles.title: 'World-class' London graffiti artist Helch dies as tributes paid from art world
articles.excerpt: Helch rose to fame in 2018 by painting his eponymous tag on a series of bridges, viaducts and rooftops
articles.content:
News | London

Allow Exco Player content

This content is provided by Exco Player and may use cookies or similar technologies. Please click 'Allow and Continue' below to load the content.

Elusive graffiti artist Helch, behind some of the most famous outdoor murals in London, has passed away - sparking a flood of tributes from the art world and on social media.

The guerrilla artist gained a reputation for painting giant block words over buildings, concrete motorway bridges and rail viaducts as well as several rooftops.

Helch first came to prominence in 2018 by painting his eponymous tag in capital letters across a string of public spots in London as well as bridges on the M4, M1 and M25.

The tag was sometimes painted in stylised fonts or different colours, and occasionally appeared just as the simple letter “H”.

His identity has never been officially revealed, although he has been named in a Daily Mail report as Michael Purdy, 34, whose work featured in a sell-out show at BSMT in Dalston, east London, at the end of last year.

Read More

Helch’s artworks did not always go down well with the public, with some motorists hitting out in anger in October 2018 when an old graffiti sign of ‘Give Peas A Chance’ was replaced on the Chalfont Viaduct on the M25 with “Give Helch A Break”.

But across the art world, Helch’s adventurous forays - usually carried out in the dead of night - led to him being dubbed “a world class artist” who “embodied everything we love about graffiti”.

In an online tribute, Alternative London posted: “We were so fortunate to witness him at work. We’ve never seen anyone do what he did before and there will never be another like him again.

“Above all he was a great human being who recently donated a share of his book sales to animal charities.

“Sending all our love and condolences to his family and loved ones. The streets of East London will never be the same again.”

News of Helch's death was shared on Instagram by BSMT.

The gallery wrote online: "Receiving news today of the untimely passing of Helch has left us broken hearted. It felt like he stepped into our lives out of the ether.

"Prompted by a moment of revelation standing outside of the American Carwash in Shoreditch - a triumph of roller graffiti and an East London landmark - I was so drawn to the enigma and mystery of the word I had to find out more.

"It took six months to get him to agree to meet in person, and in 2022 we released his first print which sold out within the hour.

"A stranger to the gallery world Helch was a true creature of the night, it’s where he found his vocation and the gallery walls were not always what it was about for him. We often had to recalibrate what this meant as we worked together.

"Over the past year his work progressed exponentially, he was coming into his own as an artist. A true perfectionist - he wouldn’t present anything that wasn’t to his standard and it was an honour to witness.

"An urban landscape without an H in it seems unfathomable. A life unlike any other, he was compelled to leave his mark on this world. There will never be another like him. Rest well H- your rollers have spoken their truth."

Fans of the artist paid tribute on X, with one describing him as a “huge part of London’s graffiti scene”.

Another wrote: “Very saddened to hear the graffiti writer Helch has passed away.

“A roller king & a nice dude - it’s hard to go anywhere in the UK without seeing a Helch or big H somewhere. Your mark will last a long long time.”

Helch’s death has not been confirmed on his website.

articles.content:
LEGO has officially unveiled one of the most anticipated sets of 2026, 21371 Wallace & Gromit, based on Aardman’s beloved claymation characters!

This 1,038-piece model lets you build a stunningly realistic model of Wallace, Gromit and their signature red motorbike that’s the perfect way to commemorate Aardman’s 50th anniversary.

21371 Wallace & Gromit will be the 10th LEGO Ideas set released in 2026, and will be launching globally on 1 October 2026 with pre-orders open now! You’ll be able to find it from LEGO.com or your local LEGO Store.

See below for international pricing and product pages if you’d like to pre-order:

  • 21371 Wallace & Gromit [AUS] – AU$149.99
  • 21371 Wallace & Gromit [UK] – £89.99
  • 21371 Wallace & Gromit [EU] – €99.99

If you’re planning on purchasing or pre-ordering this set, please consider using the affiliate links in this post. I may earn a small commission with each purchase that helps support the work I do on the blog!

The set is based on the winning model of the 90s Throwback – The Next Chapter!  challenge, by Pidelium, and I have to say, the LEGO Ideas team have done a remarkable job of staying incredibly faithful to his submission, but adding a lot of polish and fun flourishes to enhance the overall design.

For one thing, both Wallace and Gromit look super expressive, and the LEGO Ideas model also successfully mimics Aardman’s iconic claymation aesthetic with softer curves across all the characters.

The plasticine that Aardman uses for their stop-motion animations translates pretty well as an analogue to LEGO, which is a super versatile (and playful) medium that you can make near-anything out of, making this collaboration between Aardman and The LEGO Group one that just works so well together.

Gromit in particular looks fantastic, and I love that they retained the use of the LEGO magnifying glasses for his goggles, and also incorporated his flappy ears into the model.

Check out more photos supplied by LEGO below.

I think that LEGO have knocked 21371 Wallace & Gromit out of the park. The model looks phenomenal, it’s priced very decently at US$100 / AU$150 / £90 and if you’re a fan of Wallace & Gromit, you’ll know just how difficult it is to find high quality official merchandise, so this is going to be a fantastic gift or addition to your LEGO collection if you grew up watching Wallace & Gromit.

21371 Wallace & Gromit will be released on 1 October 2026, and will be available from LEGO.com or your local LEGO store.

articles.title: Artist behind iconic motorway bridge graffiti dies
articles.excerpt: The anonymous painter was known only as Helch
articles.content:
The artist behind the 'Boris is Helch' graffiti has passed away.

Helch shot to fame in 2018 when he targeted landmarks across the UK with his 'HELCH' tag in block capitals, including the blue bridge across the M4 in Bristol which, confusingly, was tagged 'Boris is Helch'.

The anonymous artist evoked the spirit of Banksy in Bristol, with the tag ranging from colourful and artistic, to plain lettering, to simply a large, decorated 'H'.

The London-based art gallery BMST Space confirmed the news, saying it had left them "broken-hearted".

"It felt like he stepped into our lives out of the ether," the account stated on Instagram.

"It took six months to get him to agree to meet in person, and in 2022 we released his first print which sold out within the hour. A stranger to the gallery world, Helch was a true creature of the night, it’s where he found his vocation and the gallery walls were not always what it was about for him. We often had to recalibrate what this meant as we worked together.

"Over the past year his work progressed exponentially, he was coming into his own as an artist. A true perfectionist - he wouldn’t present anything that wasn’t to his standard and it was an honour to witness.

"An urban landscape without an H in it seems unfathomable. A life unlike any other, he was compelled to leave his mark on this world. There will never be another like him."

In 2019, Bristolians were baffled when 'Helch' appeared on a bridge over M4 to the north of the city. In July, someone had painted the words 'Boris is...' on the eastern side of the bridge, visible to westbound traffic.

It didn't indicate which Boris the graffiti was referring to. The work remained up for several weeks, and caused something of a stir on social media before being painted over by Network Rail. Then the words 'Boris is Helch' appeared.

MyLondon investigated, and spoke to someone who claimed to know who ‘Helch’ was.

They claimed he was an old school graffiti tagger who had suddenly, in middle-age, gone back to his youth and begun painting the name ‘Helch’. MyLondon’s source said: "It was just a name that he picked. It's got no real significance, it's just his tag."

articles.title: New Comics This Week: Full Comics List For September 2, 2026 | Comic Book Club
articles.excerpt: Looking for a list of new comics this week? Here's what's coming to comic book stores on September 2, 2026 from DC Comics, Marvel, Image and more.
articles.content:
• News

New month, new comics, let’s goooo!! And this is a particularly great week with a slew of new books coming at you for September 2, 2026. So let’s get into some highlights for what’s coming to comic book stores, then the full list of single issues.

DC has a packed week led by three Next Level titles: Legion of Super-Heroes #1, Doom Patrol #1 and Teen Titans #1. That would be more than enough (they’re all be crackling good teams), but they’ve also got Superman: The Stranger #1, a Black Label book by Wes Craig going back to the Man of Steel’s origin. And also there’s Batman/Superman/Weird Al: World’s Weirdest, which sends Al to save Batman and Superman.

Marvel, meanwhile, celebrates a few anniversaries with the Spider-Woman 50th Anniversary Special, featuring a new story by Ann Nocenti and one by Dan Watters setting up the future. Marvel Mangaverse: Web of Blood #1 kicks off a month-long event celebrating the 25th anniversary of the Mangaverse. And Black Panther / Namor: Doomed #1 sends three kings to hell.

Speaking of which, BOOM! Studios opens the puzzle box with Hellraiser: Resurrections – New Wounds #1. Dark Horse Comics expands the origin of the title character in The Perfectly Monstrous Life of Adam Frankenstein #1 from Tate Brombal and Soo Lee. And Oni Press brings on a brand new Archie #1.

Looking for previous lists? Check out our New Comics This Week archive for back-lists of comics, so you can get caught up quickly.

Read on for the full list of new comics this week from DC Comics, Marvel, Image Comics, and beyond.
